A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VladVA research, with the same authors, core method and principal experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material support reliable comparison, including content moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval, compositionality and ImageNet results, component ablations, representation analyses and qualitative captioning examples, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V3 retains the original empirical results and additionally reports VLM2Vec comparisons, training-data scaling results and summary-token layer sensitivity.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same shared LVLM/LLM embedding architecture, contrastive training on short captions, autoregressive training on long captions, soft prompts and LoRA adapters. V3 clarifies prompts, token notation and training versus inference; these edits do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: The retrieval, compositionality, ImageNet and qualitative captioning coverage is retained. V3 documents OpenImages, CC3M and ShareGPT-4V as the composition of the previously reported 8.1M training pool, without establishing a replacement of that pool. Its new size and layer studies use existing benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 add VLM2Vec (Mistral-7B) and remove CLIP (ViT-B) from the corresponding retrieval, SugarCrepe and SugarCrepe++ comparisons. CLIP (ViT-B) remains in the supplementary Winoground and ImageNet comparisons. Other comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: V3 adds training-size and mixture conditions in Table 5 and evaluates summary-token layers 32, 31, 28, 24, 20 and 16 in Table 11. Existing benchmark splits and metrics remain unchanged. Newly stated optimization settings document the training recipe rather than establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends the ablation coverage with two previously absent questions: how performance changes as training data grows and its composition changes (Section 5.2, Table 5), and how performance depends on the summary-token layer (supplementary Section 10, Table 11). Existing component, prompt, architecture and captioning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained embedding-variance and entropy analyses do not introduce a change in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V3 adds VLM2Vec results and substantive data-scaling and layer-sensitivity results; Table 11 reports layer-16 changes of -59.0 on Flickr30k and -20.0 on SugarCrepe relative to the last layer. Retained methods' benchmark scores are unchanged. V3 also corrects prose to match existing tables: SugarCrepe object swap 85.8 to 79.0, and retrieval gains over E5-V from 6 to 7 points on COCO and 6.2 to 6.4 on nocaps.

T1.justification: The contrastive and autoregressive objectives retain their mathematical substance. Added modality and long-caption superscripts clarify existing variables. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v3 adds none.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: converting generative LVLMs into discriminative models through combined objectives and parameter-efficient adaptation, with improved retrieval and compositionality. The additional evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the scaling results as showing no immediate saturation and motivates last-layer extraction through greater adaptation capacity, while noting similar performance among late layers. Section 3.2.3 also corrects the caption-diversity explanation from a property that does not naturally emerge to one that does. Existing ImageNet and text-only compositionality qualifications remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds a substantial training recipe absent from v1: dataset composition, five BLIP2 captions per OpenImages image with one sampled during training, caption augmentation details, LoRA rank and alpha of 16, prompt-length selection, seven epochs, batch size 1024, learning rate 1e-4, AdamW without weight decay, cosine scheduling, up to 32 A100 GPUs, and PyTorch/DeepSpeed implementation.

R1.justification: V3 adds VLM2Vec as concurrent work and explicitly distinguishes its training from VladVA's generative loss, short/long-caption strategy and soft prompting. Additional references cover domain-specific pretraining, training datasets, optimization and software. The broader positioning against CLIP-like models and E5-V remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title gains the VladVA name, Section 3 gains a roadmap, and several method passages receive clearer wording and notation explanations. V3 also explicitly separates supplementary material. The principal narrative and section sequence remain recognizable rather than being extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to distinguish contrastive and autoregressive training. V3 adds Tables 5 and 11, changes comparator rows in Tables 1–3, relocates Figure 3 and reorganizes supplementary pagination. Most existing plots, tables and qualitative displays retain their visual structure and content.

improvement.justification: V1 omits essential training-data and optimization information; v3's Section 4 substantially remedies this reproducibility deficiency. The added LVLM comparator and two sensitivity studies also strengthen assessment of the unchanged method. The scaling study changes data composition alongside sample count, limiting its interpretation as a pure size effect, but this limitation does not outweigh the substantial documentation and validation gains.
